_meta.note: The technology program. Each node is cash plus time, and delivers a permanent change to operating conditions — the same mechanism events use, just with no expiry. Adding a node is a JSON entry.
_meta.shape: cost is paid up front; the node lands `quarters` later and never lapses. `requires` gates a node behind another, which is what makes it a tree rather than a shopping list.
_meta.effects: Same vocabulary as the event deck: fuelPrice, demand, fare, maintenanceCost, crewCost, handlingCost, completion. A node that improves something uses a multiplier below 1 for costs and above 1 for revenue. `loadCeiling` raises how much of the aircraft a carrier can actually fill on a sector that is turning traffic away — revenue management, capacity planning and repeat custom all do this in reality, and without it every strong route flew at exactly the same load factor forever.
_meta.calibration: Effects are deliberately small. Delivering the whole tree is worth roughly 12% on fare and demand and about 10% off the main cost lines — a real margin improvement for a several-hundred-million program, but not a different game. At double these values the tree was worth ~27 points of margin and a fully-teched carrier could not lose. Costs were raised ~30% and lead times ~35% (2026-07-22): the full tree runs ~$570M and the longest node lands two years out, so technology is a real multi-year commitment rather than a formality a rich carrier clears in passing. Harder access, same per-node effects.
